overall: Joint letter to the Danvers Planning Board and Conservation Commission: no Open Meeting Law violation found for email/phone-only public comment or remote participation; the public hearing claim was declined as outside the OML.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the virtual meeting barred real-time public participation because comment came only by email or phone, not verbally during the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body provide such opportunity but rather gives discretion to the chair of a public body to determine who may speak or otherwise participate at a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged failure to allow public participation as required by Section 3 of the COVID-19 Executive Order, which requires remote appearances for parties before the body.
allegations.key_passage: Both the Board and the Commission provided the public with adequate, alternative access to the remote meeting via a live broadcast on YouTube and local television.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the virtual hearings violated the requirement for active, real-time public participation in public hearings under the Executive Order and hearing laws.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review, and offer no opinion on, whether any actions taken by the Board or Commission could be a violation of any public hearing law or regulation, including the above provision of the Executive Order.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
